name: Italian Sausage and Peppers Skillet

fit.note: Numbers themselves clear the band: 476 cal in [400,650]; 12g carb <=35g; no seafood; skillet scales to 14 by weigh-and-divide; budget pork-sausage plate. FIT on conditions, but killed as a pool-dupe below.

dupe_check.evidence: Structurally identical to pool candidate 'italian-sausage-peppers-onions-skillet' (already ruled KEEP by another adjudicator, verdict landed): both are Italian sausage links + bell peppers + onions, no starch base, cooked in a skillet with garlic/herb/vinegar seasoning. All four identity axes match - protein (italian sausage), flavor family (Italian), starch (none), method (skillet). This is the same dinner. Against the live catalog it is NOT a dupe (catalog only has sausage-and-peppers on a pasta base: italian-sausage-penne, orecchiette-italian-sausage-broccoli, spicy-italian-sausage-orzo), so the collision is purely with the pool twin.
dupe_check.loser_rationale: This slice is the weaker of the twin pair: 476 cal / 12g carb vs the twin's 420 cal / 8g carb, and it carries no distinguishing feature (same source-type single-skillet keto plate). Keep the twin, cut this one.

borderline.reason: Not borderline against the catalog. The only issue is the exact pool duplicate, and the tie-break is clear (twin has better numbers), so this is a clean pool-dupe cut, not a borderline hold.

cross_protein_collisions: Same-dish-different-protein risk: any low-carb TURKEY sausage + peppers + onions skillet, or CHICKEN sausage + peppers + onions skillet, in another selector's pool is the same plate as the surviving twin. Catalog already has rice-based turkey-sausage-and-peppers; a no-rice turkey/chicken twin would collide with italian-sausage-peppers-onions-skillet. Orchestrator merge pass should keep only one 'sausage and peppers no-starch skillet' across all proteins.
